fatal_errors: The proposed nanohierarchical composition-undulation intervention is undefined and does not reconstruct the controlled variation of Mo content in the Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3-containing composites.
The baseline is incorrectly treated as bare CoCrFeNi rather than the Mo0.2 composite with fixed lubricant and oxide additions.
No supporting prior evidence is cited.
The mechanism omits Mo-induced lattice distortion, sigma-phase strengthening, low-temperature MoS2/Ag lubrication, and high-temperature oxide/silver-molybdate glaze formation.

The experiment lacks a specified architecture, matched processing controls, counterface, load, speed, distance, atmosphere, and measurements capable of identifying the proposed structural and tribofilm mediators.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the broad challenge of dry sliding from room temperature to 800 °C and predicts lower friction and wear, but nearly all target-specific scientific content is absent. It substitutes a vague architectural intervention for Mo-content tuning in a multicomponent self-lubricating composite, uses the wrong baseline, and provides only generic contact-stress and tribofilm claims. Its high-temperature-only falsification rule also cannot establish performance throughout the full range and would miss the important 200–400 °C friction and wear maxima. Without citations, quantitative boundaries, structural characterization, or a reproducible definition of the intervention, it is neither an evidence-supported alternative nor a reconstruction.
